key_insight: LLM agents can act as a practical natural-language interface for home energy scheduling, achieving near-optimal multi-appliance control when connected to live pricing, weather, and generation tools.
engineering_relevance: This points to a deployable path for turning household preferences into automated, cost-aware control policies for demand response and solar self-consumption.
method: Tool-calling ReAct agent with native function calling
Uses live Octopus Agile prices, weather forecasts, PV estimates, and household usage data
Benchmarked against MILP ground truth and week-long deployment scenarios
evidence_signal: Across tariff, conflict, and weather-aware tests, GPT-4o-mini, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and Claude Sonnet 4.6 reached 100% scheduling success with native function calling and captured 96.7–98.0% of oracle savings over a simulated week.
watch_item: Results depend on reliable tool access and structured function calling; text-parsed action interfaces reduced reliability sharply, which may limit robustness in real homes.
paper_title: LLMs for Agentic Home Energy Management
